title: Best Ways to Get to Singapore with Points
body:
The best ways to get to Singapore with points are a Qantas Classic Flight Reward from 29,000 points one-way in Economy, a Velocity Reward Seat on Singapore Airlines from 29,000 points, or a KrisFlyer Saver award on Singapore Airlines’ own program. All three programs use fixed award tables for this route. A Membership Rewards balance (American Express’s transferable points currency) can also be transferred to each program. Sydney to Singapore covers about 3,908 flown miles. The distance determines the award price in each program. Here is what the route costs across the programs in 2026. We also explain how each option works in practice.
What Singapore costs in points across the programs in 2026
Three programs use fixed charts to price awards between Australia and Singapore. The minimum award prices are closer together than the programs’ reputations might suggest. The table below compares one-way prices from the East Coast as of September 2026. Prices are per passenger and exclude taxes, fees, and carrier charges.
Program and airline Economy Business Qantas Frequent Flyer, Qantas aircraft 29,000 82,100 Velocity, Singapore Airlines 29,000 74,000 KrisFlyer Saver, Singapore Airlines from 29,000 72,000
Each program adds its own cash component. Qantas shows taxes, fees and carrier charges at booking. Singapore Airlines’ bookings through Velocity add carrier charges in United States dollars. KrisFlyer awards include taxes and charges payable separately. The points price is the start of the comparison, not the end.
The Qantas Frequent Flyer path to Singapore
Qantas prices Singapore in the 3,601-4,800 mile band of its Classic Flight Reward tables , which have applied to bookings from 5 August 2025. On Qantas aircraft, the one-way prices are 29,000 points in Economy, 61,600 in Premium Economy and 82,100 in Business Class. A return in Business Class costs 164,200 points. Reward seats are capacity-controlled and not guaranteed until booked. No booking fee applies when redeeming online, and taxes, fees and carrier charges are quoted at the time of booking. 2 identical bookings can carry different cash components on different dates. The Premium Economy row is worth knowing too, at 61,600 points one-way in the same band.
This path’s strength lies in the network and earning engine behind it. Qantas Points flow from the top Qantas Points-earning credit cards , the wider ways to earn Qantas Points , and periodic transfer bonus promotions , so a household already earning into Qantas usually reaches this route first. The route also anchors bigger plans. The same 3,601-4,800 mile band prices every major Southeast Asian gateway, which means a Singapore-sized balance is really an Asia-sized balance.
The Velocity path on Singapore Airlines
Velocity books Singapore Airlines Reward Seats from a dedicated partner chart. Sydney to Singapore falls in its 3,601-4,200 mile band at 29,000 points one-way in Economy and 74,000 in Business Class under the pricing introduced on 21 January 2025. Singapore Airlines adds carrier charges of US$40 one-way in Economy and US$120 in Business Class on flights up to 4,200 miles. These are payable on top of Velocity’s taxes and fees.
The appeal here is the aircraft. The booking puts you on Singapore Airlines aircraft in its own long-haul cabins for fewer points than Qantas Business Class. The balance comes from the top Velocity Points earning credit cards and the bank programs that transfer into Velocity . This path may suit a traveller who specifically wants a Singapore Airlines cabin and holds a flexible bank currency. This is because the points price is lower than the Qantas figure, while the Singapore Airlines seat quality carries the trip.
The KrisFlyer path and how bank points feed all three
KrisFlyer is Singapore Airlines’ own program, and its Saver chart, effective 1 November 2025, prices the airline’s East Coast Australia flights at 72,000 miles one-way in Business Class, with Economy from about 29,000 miles. Saver awards release in limited numbers and are bookable up to 355 days ahead. A round trip prices at double the one-way figure and includes one complimentary stopover of up to 30 days. Taxes and charges are payable separately in cash. The program suits a traveller committed to the airline itself, because the miles carry a 3-year expiry once they arrive that no amount of activity resets, which makes speculative transfers less suitable.
Warning: choosing between the three programs is a multi-step calculation. The transfer ratio is the step people skip
Price the seat in each program first. The one-way Business Class prices as of September 2026 are 82,100, 74,000 and 72,000 points or miles
Then price the currency. Membership Rewards converts at 2:1 into Qantas or Velocity, but 3:1 into KrisFlyer. That means 72,000 KrisFlyer miles cost 216,000 bank points, compared with 148,000 for the Velocity seat
Add each program’s cash charges before deciding, because a lower points price can come with higher cash charges
For most Australians, the points currency they already earn will determine the route. The Membership Rewards transfer guide maps the ratios, and the benchmark values in the December 2025 rewards points valuations update provide a reference for judging whichever seat appears.
Frequently asked questions
Which program is cheapest for Business Class to Singapore? +
The chart minimums sit within about 10,000 points of one another. As of September 2026, it will cost 72,000 KrisFlyer miles, 74,000 Velocity Points, or 82,100 Qantas Points one way. The real answer depends on which currency you already hold, the cash charges on each ticket, and whether a seat exists on your dates. The cheapest program on paper isn’t always the cheapest trip.
How many points do I need for a return in Economy? +
From 58,000 in either Qantas Points or Velocity Points, since both programs price the East Coast route from 29,000 points each way. KrisFlyer’s Economy Saver pricing sits in the same region, from about 29,000 miles each way, before each program’s taxes and charges.
Do the three programs release the same seats? +
No. Each program draws on its own reward inventory, so a date with nothing bookable through one program can show seats in another. Checking all the currencies you can reach before transferring anything is part of the booking, and how the partner programs interlock explains the relationships.
Is Premium Economy a smart middle option? +
On Qantas aircraft, it is priced at 61,600 points one-way in the Singapore band, roughly double Economy and three-quarters of the way to Business Class. It suits a traveller who values extra room but cannot find or afford a Business Class seat. Availability follows the same capacity controls as the other cabins.
Fees, rates and figures quoted are correct at the time of publication and should be verified directly with each provider before acting on them.
